# Central Command Representative
1. Central Command Representatives represent Central Command and all interests and values of the company. They are on station to ensure compliance with Corporate Policy, as well as to advise Command Staff in matters pertaining to the Station.
2. If members of Command Staff demonstrate behavior unbecoming of their role, it is the Representative’s duty to issue written warnings and, if necessary, have them removed from their positions.
3. If there is no Captain on the station, it is the duty of the Representative to promote a temporary Captain from the Command Staff until a replacement arrives. Should no Command Staff be willing to take the role, Representatives are authorized to act as a Captain until such a time as one arrives.
4. Barring extenuating circumstances provided in Sections 2 and 3, the Representative role aboard the station is purely advisory. Discipline should be carried out by the Security Team and Magistrate.
5. Should circumstances arise in which extenuating circumstances must be applied (such as those from Sections 2 and 3), a fax must be sent out to Central Command to notify them of the situation. Should the situation be a dire emergency, the Red Phone may be utilized, but it is highly preferred to use faxes for recordkeeping purposes. Further, if the phone is used, the Representative will be expected to fill out a full situation report and have it faxed after the emergency has been resolved.
6. Any sensitive documents within the Central Command Representative's possession at the start of the shift are to be kept secure. Central Command is to be contacted should any of these documents go missing.
7. It is the responsibility of the Representative to serve as a bridge between the crew and Central Command. Central Command correspondences from non-Central Command personnel must bear the CCR Stamp to be considered valid.
